name: McLaughlin Hall
use: Residence hall, 127 first-year students; Health & Human Services learning community

renovations.what: Domestic hot water to be supplied from a new shared steam-fired heater in Congreve (bid); McLaughlin keeps a gas instantaneous heater as backup

facts.text: Dedicated March 19, 1955, and named for Helen Fitch McLaughlin, chair of home economics from 1920, who served UNH for 36 years.
Small first-year hall of 127 students at 32 Ballard Street, on a hill overlooking western campus and surrounded by trees and lawns.
Has a gender-inclusive community restroom on the ground floor and a single-use restroom on the first floor; lounges on all floors.

photos.caption: Gable end and side on its wooded hillside

s3.title: UNH Congreve Hall Heat Exchanger Replacement (bid notice, published 2024-05-25)

verdict: Small 1955 brick hall on a wooded hill; quiet and well staffed, little else.
notes: CONTRADICTION: the McLaughlin hall page lists 'Air conditioning' under Amenities, but UNH Housing's air-conditioning facility tag does not include McLaughlin (it lists ATW, Congreve, Fairchild, Haaland, Handler, Mills, Peterson). Old row said no A/C; left 'unknown'. Architect not given by the archives. Hall size is 127 now (old row ~123). Photos: three-storey red-brick Colonial Revival-style block with white trim, pedimented entry and a stair up a leafy slope; lobby interior is dated (painted trim, glass doors). Licensed photo (2013): a plain three-storey red-brick box with a low gable roof and regular double-hung windows on a grassy hillside under pines; modest and well kept.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a neat gabled brick block.
